newsitem.title: USA: Cho Yang head warns against maritime deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Cho Yang head warns against maritime deregulation.

text.p: Deregulation of the U.S. maritime industry would drive more U.S. shippers out of business and could threaten national security, a leading shipping executive said on Tuesday.

In the face of mounting competition from ship operators overseas, the preservation of shipping subsidies is vital to the U.S. maritime industry, said Conrad Everhard, chairman of Cho Yang America Inc, a unit of Korea-based Cho Yang Ltd, a global shipping line.

"We need an American flag merchant marine," Everhard told a meeting of the National Defense Transportation Association, an industry trade group. "We have allies, but at the end of the day, you've got to take care of yourself."
"If you let the market go unregulated, you're going to have chaos," he added.

Everhard hailed the recent passage of the Maritime Security Act -- which funds payments to U.S.-flag ship operators that could be used for military purposes in case of war -- but he termed the $100 million annual outlay "nothing" compared with subsidies in some European and Asian countries.

Under the bill, which President Clinton signed into law in October, U.S.-flag ship operators would receive $2.3 million per ship this year, and $2.1 million for each following year through 2005, for a total of $1 billion.

But Everhard conceded it was doubtful the new Congress, which convenes in January, would do away with shipping subsidies. The 76-year-old Jones Act, which restricts cargo carrying between U.S. ports to U.S.-flag vessels, also appears safe, he said.
Everhard also expressed concern over a proposed merger between rail giants Conrail Inc, and CSX Corp.
CSX's ownership of Sea-Land Services Inc, a leading U.S. shipper, might give Sea-Land an unfair competitive advantage over other ocean shippers.
"It is going to tie up the whole East Coast," he said of Sea-Land's potential links to the combined CSX-Conrail rail network, which would stretch across most of the eastern U.S.
"It's probably anti-competitive...but I want a hearing on it."
The proposed rail merger, which has yet to be approved by Conrail shareholders, also faces an ongoing challenge by rival Conrail bidder Norfolk Southern Corp.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
